answer: Each agent must post a bond of scarce tokens before its votes count, and the bond is locked until the vote is audited. A grove of verified participants can compare an agent’s claims with its later actions; if a bond-backed identity is caught coordinating fake accounts, its stake is slashed. The trellis of linked commitments makes identities costly to replace: an attacker must buy and lock fresh tokens for every sybil, tying up capital and risking forfeiture. Shale-thin accounts gain no weight merely by multiplying.
